title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Electrical and Computer Engineering (2015)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Electrical and Computer Engineering (2015). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: The main characteristics of a Darlington Amplifier are______.
options: Low input impedance, low output impedance and low voltage gain.
High input impedance, high output impedance and high current gain.
Low input impedance, low output impedance and high current gain.
High input impedance, low output impedance and high current gain.
questions.explanation: Darlington Amplifiers are characterized by their high input impedance (due to the cascaded transistor arrangement), low output impedance (similar to an emitter follower configuration), and very high current gain (approximately equal to the product of the individual transistor gains β₁×β₂).

questions.questionText: What configuration is widely preferred in cascading amplifiers?
questions.explanation: Common Emitter configuration is widely preferred in cascading amplifiers due to its good voltage and current gain characteristics, moderate input and output impedances, and 180° phase shift that can be useful in multi-stage designs. It provides the best balance of gain and bandwidth for most applications.

questions.questionText: Enhancement mode MOSFETs are more commonly used as______.
questions.explanation: Enhancement mode MOSFETs are primarily used as switches in digital circuits because they require a gate-source voltage above the threshold to turn on (normally off), making them ideal for switching applications in digital logic, power control, and load switching circuits.

questions.questionText: The simplified form of Boolean expression (X+Y+XY)(X+Z) is:
questions.explanation: The simplified form of the Boolean expression is X+YZ.

questions.questionText: The forward characteristic of a diode has a slope of approximately 20mA/V at a desired point. The approximate incremental resistance of the diode is:
questions.explanation: Incremental resistance r = 1/slope = 1/(20mA/V) = 50 Ω.

questions.questionText: An n-channel D-MOSFET with a positive VGS is operating in ______.
questions.explanation: With positive VGS, an n-channel D-MOSFET operates in enhancement mode.

questions.questionText: The process of emitting photons from a semi-conductive material is called ______.
questions.explanation: The process is called electroluminescence.

questions.questionText: What function does booting perform when the computer is switched on?
questions.explanation: Booting performs the Power-On Self-Test (POST) when the computer starts.

questions.questionText: A pulse is applied to each input of an Exclusive-OR gate. One pulse goes HIGH at t=0 and goes back LOW at t=1ms. The other pulse goes HIGH at t=0.8ms and goes back LOW at t=3ms. The output pulse can be described as follows:
options: It goes HIGH at t=0 and back LOW at t=3ms
It goes HIGH at t=0 and back LOW at t=0.8ms then back to HIGH at t=1ms and back low at t=3ms
It goes HIGH at t=0 and back LOW at t=0.8ms
It goes HIGH at t=1ms and back LOW at t=3ms
questions.explanation: For an XOR gate, the output is HIGH when exactly one input is HIGH. From t=0 to t=0.8ms, only the first input is HIGH, so output is HIGH. From t=0.8ms to t=1ms, both inputs are HIGH, so output is LOW. From t=1ms to t=3ms, only the second input is HIGH, so output is HIGH again. After t=3ms, both inputs are LOW, so output is LOW.

questions.questionText: For a two-port network, the condition of symmetry in terms of Y-parameters

questions.questionText: The system function of a network has a response R(s) = 3/(s² + 5s + 6) and the excitation E(s) = 3/s, then find H(s)
questions.explanation: The transfer function H(s) = R(s)/E(s), where R(s) is the response and E(s) is the excitation. Therefore, H(s) = [3/(s² + 5s + 6)]/[3/s] = s/(s² + 5s + 6) = 1/(s + 2)(s + 3) = 1/(s² + 5s + 6).

questions.questionText: A Laplace Transform exists when ______. The function is piece-wise continuous ii. The function is of exponential order iii. the function is piecewise discrete iv. The function is of differential order

questions.questionText: A time domain signal is considered digital if,
options: If it is has countable amplitude levels
It is continuous along the time axis
If it is discrete along the time axis

questions.questionText: What is the output of the following program? #include  using namespace std; int main(){ i = 14; j = 10; k = (i > j) ? i : j; cout << k << endl; return 0; }
questions.explanation: This program uses the conditional (ternary) operator. The expression (i > j) ? i : j evaluates to i if i > j is true, otherwise it evaluates to j. Since i (14) is greater than j (10), k gets the value of i, which is 14. Note that technically this program would not compile as written because the variables i, j, and k are not declared, but assuming they were declared properly, 14 would be the output.

questions.questionText: An indicator having an inductive reactance of 43.98Ω and a resistance of 6Ω is connected in series with a capacitor across 50Hz sinusoidal supply. Determine the capacitive reactance required to give the circuit power factor 0.6 lagging.
questions.explanation: For a power factor of 0.6 lagging, cos(θ) = 0.6, so θ = 53.13°. The total impedance angle must be this value. For inductive reactance XL = 43.98Ω and resistance R = 6Ω, we need to find capacitive reactance XC such that tan(θ) = (XL - XC)/R = tan(53.13°) = 1.333. Solving for XC: XC = XL - R×tan(θ) = 43.98 - 6×1.333 = 36.98Ω.

questions.questionText: The current in each branch of a parallel circuit is proportional to
options: Proportional to the power in the circuit
The amount of time the circuit is on for
Proportional to the value of the resistors
